1.lede: A one-month prospecting campaign for a Brainbox Associate — targeting WA residential builders, renovators and specialist trade contractors that carry heavy administrative load and tight local labour supply.
1.whyPressure: Quoting, take-offs, supplier follow-up, project scheduling, variation tracking, invoice chasing and client updates all compete with the work that actually protects margin on site. Owners, supervisors, estimators and project managers absorb this admin themselves because another senior local hire is slow and expensive.
1.whyOpp: The strongest use case is not replacing site-based people. It is giving the local team reliable support for the recurring work that slows them down between jobs — so throughput improves without adding local overhead. The best entry product is a dedicated project administration, estimating support or scheduling assistant.
1.marketShape: Fragmented at the SME level with no single dominant player — ideal for outreach. Avoid the major builders and target 10–80 person builders, renovators and specialist trade contractors (electrical, plumbing, fabrication and fit-out).

ie.h1: The labour market they live in
ie.p1: WA residential building and specialist trades have ridden a long demand wave straight into a persistent skills shortage. Competition for licensed tradespeople, supervisors and estimators is intense, and the same shortage extends to the office: good construction administrators, contracts and scheduling staff are hard to find, slow to recruit and expensive to keep.
ie.p2: Building is a high-transaction, document-heavy business. A single job generates quotes, take-offs, purchase orders, supplier follow-ups, variations, RFIs, compliance paperwork, progress claims, invoices and constant client updates. In a 10–80 person firm there is rarely a deep back office, so it lands on owners, supervisors, estimators and project managers doing admin at night — time not spent winning or pricing work.
ie.p3: Margins are tight. Years of materials and labour cost inflation, fixed-price contracts signed before costs rose, and well-publicised construction insolvencies have made owners cost-conscious and cautious about fixed overhead. Slow quote turnaround loses jobs, poor supplier follow-up delays sites, and weak invoicing strangles cash flow.
ie.p4: The credible message is separation of work, not replacement of people. Licensed, on-site and client-facing work stays local; the repeatable back-office process work can be handled by a dedicated, trained, supervised offshore team member at a fraction of a local hire — capacity and cash-flow relief, not cost-cutting.
ie.p5: Know the language: take-offs, variations, RFIs, progress claims, retentions, defects, practical completion, PC/PS items. Know the tools: Buildxact, Databuild, Simpro, ServiceM8, procore, Xero, MYOB. Listen first and name the one workflow that clearly hurts most.

2.lede: A one-month campaign targeting WA allied health, NDIS and private specialist clinics — providers under constant pressure to protect clinical quality while intake, billing and admin pile up around the clinicians.
2.entry: Clinic administration assistant (intake, billing, reminders, document workflows)
2.whyPressure: Clinics must maintain service quality while managing intake, scheduling, billing, report administration, referral follow-up and client communication. Most don't need another clinician to fix that — they need stronger administrative capacity around the clinicians they already have.
2.whyOpp: The best offshore use cases are structured and process-driven: intake, scheduling, NDIS plan admin, billing support, referral tracking, document formatting and client follow-up — support around clinicians without touching clinical judgement, treatment decisions or regulated responsibilities.
2.marketShape: Not dominated at the small-provider level. Target speech therapy, occupational therapy, psychology, physiotherapy, podiatry and multi-disciplinary clinics, and small-to-mid NDIS providers with recurring intake and plan administration.

ie.h1: The labour market they live in
ie.p1: Allied health and disability services are among WA's fastest-growing sectors, but demand has outrun the supply of both clinicians and experienced practice administrators. Clinics compete hard for reception, intake and billing staff, and turnover in those roles is high — every departure disrupts the schedule and the cash flow.
ie.p2: Clinical revenue depends on a chain of administration: intake and consent, scheduling and reminders, Medicare and private billing, NDIS plan management, service agreements, referral follow-up and report formatting. When admin slips, cancellations rise, claims stall, debtors grow and clinicians end up doing paperwork instead of billable client work.
ie.p3: NDIS pricing and compliance change frequently, margins are thin, and no-shows and unbilled sessions hit small clinics hard. Owner-clinicians often carry the practice-management load themselves, and burnout is real. They want to see more clients without adding another expensive local hire.
ie.p4: Clinical judgement, treatment and regulated decisions stay with the local team. A dedicated offshore administrator handles the structured, process-driven work — intake, reminders, billing, referral tracking, document formatting and debtor follow-up — improving clinic flow and freeing clinicians for client care.
ie.p5: Know the language: intake, triage, plan management, service agreements, self-managed vs plan-managed vs agency-managed, NDIS line items, Medicare EPC, DVA, no-shows and DNAs. Know the tools: Cliniko, Halaxy, Coreplus, Splose, PowerDiary. Respect privacy and clinical boundaries in every sentence.

3.lede: A one-month campaign targeting WA mining-services and METS SMEs — suppliers to the resources sector carrying large-client expectations without large-company back-office support.
3.entry: Mobilisation / procurement / HSEQ document-control or maintenance-planning assistant
3.whyPressure: Mobilisation, procurement follow-up, HSEQ document control, maintenance administration, tender support and reporting absorb the time of managers who need to stay focused on delivery. These suppliers face major-client standards without the internal shared-service structure of a major.
3.whyOpp: The strongest use case is structured operational support: document control, procurement admin, mobilisation tracking, timesheet processing, maintenance-planning support, reporting and CRM discipline — supporting the people who keep the work moving, not replacing field capability.
3.marketShape: Avoid the mining majors. Target the suppliers to mining — services, maintenance, fabrication, equipment and HSEQ-adjacent businesses — which have volume, urgency and fewer internal shared-service resources.

ie.h1: The labour market they live in
ie.p1: WA's resources economy keeps demand for mining-services labour high and wages higher. METS SMEs compete with the majors for both site crews and the office staff — schedulers, procurement officers, document controllers — who keep contracts compliant. FIFO patterns and remote sites make local administrative hiring even harder.
ie.p2: Supplying to mining means meeting big-company standards: HSEQ document control, mobilisation packs, pre-quals, timesheets, procurement follow-up, maintenance records, tender submissions and reporting. A services SME rarely has a shared-service team, so this lands on operations managers and coordinators — pulling them off delivery and putting contract compliance at risk.
ie.p3: Work comes in urgent, high-volume peaks tied to shutdowns, mobilisations and contract wins. Client audits and pre-qualification are unforgiving on documentation. Cost pressure from principals is constant, and every hour a coordinator spends chasing paperwork is an hour not spent winning or delivering the next job.
ie.p4: Field capability and site decisions stay local. A dedicated offshore resource handles the structured back-office load — HSEQ registers, mobilisation admin, procurement follow-up, timesheet processing, maintenance-planning support and reporting — keeping documentation and responsiveness consistent through the peaks.
ie.p5: Know the language: mobilisation, pre-quals, HSEQ, JHA/JSA, SWMS, shutdowns, mob/demob, plant and equipment registers, POs and variations. Know the tools: Pronto, Pegasus/Avetta, CargoWise-adjacent systems, SharePoint document control. Speak to compliance and responsiveness, not cheap labour.

4.lede: A one-month campaign targeting WA project consultancies — engineering, surveying, planning and environmental firms whose senior technical staff are pulled into drafting, formatting and admin.

4.whyPressure: Clients expect fast, polished project output, while senior technical staff are pulled into drafting, formatting, data clean-up, proposal support and document administration that could be handled elsewhere.

It is building production support around the technical team — CAD/GIS support, report formatting, QA checklist admin, proposal support, CRM updating and project admin — so they spend more time reviewing, advising and delivering.
4.marketShape: Fragmented below the tier-one firms. Target 5–50 person consultancies with recurring project deadlines across civil, structural, surveying, town planning and environmental disciplines.

ie.h1: The labour market they live in
ie.p1: Engineers, surveyors, GIS analysts and environmental scientists are in short supply across WA, and consultancies compete with government, mining and tier-one firms for the same graduates. Senior technical staff are the scarcest resource of all, which makes it painful when they spend hours on drafting and formatting instead of billable technical work.
ie.p2: Project delivery is a production line: drafting and take-offs, map preparation, report writing and formatting, QA checklists, tender and proposal documents, data clean-up and project tracking. Much of it is essential but low-leverage, and when it lands on technical staff, utilisation and margin fall while deadlines get tighter.
ie.p3: Work arrives in deadline-driven peaks tied to approvals, tenders and project milestones. Fixed-fee scopes punish inefficiency, and hard-to-resource peaks force senior staff into production work or overtime. Winning more work means more proposals — more admin — on top of delivery.
ie.p4: Professional judgement and Australian sign-off always stay local. A dedicated offshore resource builds production capacity around the technical team — drafting support, GIS assistance, report formatting, QA admin, proposal support and project tracking — lifting output without changing accountability.
ie.p5: Know the language: drafting, mark-ups, take-offs, QA/QC, RFIs, deliverables registers, approvals, referrals, scopes and variations. Know the tools: AutoCAD, Civil 3D, Revit, 12d, ArcGIS/QGIS, Bluebeam, project management systems. Emphasise technical control staying in Australia.

5.lede: A one-month campaign targeting WA transport, logistics and warehousing SMEs — operators carrying a heavy back-office load around dispatch, POD, compliance and customer updates.

ie.h1: The labour market they live in
ie.p1: Transport competes for drivers first, but the office is just as stretched — allocators, dispatch, compliance and accounts roles are hard to fill and easy to lose. WA's distances and 24/7 operating windows mean the admin never really stops, and after-hours coverage is a constant headache for lean teams.
ie.p2: Every load generates dispatch instructions, proof-of-delivery capture, customer updates, compliance and fatigue records, invoicing and job data entry. When this backs up, invoices go out late, customers chase updates, compliance registers fall behind and operational staff are pulled off moving freight to fix paperwork.
ie.p3: Margins are thin and fuel, wages and compliance costs keep rising. Chain-of-responsibility and fatigue obligations are unforgiving, and late invoicing hurts cash flow. Customers expect real-time updates that a busy allocator can't always give — so service and cash both suffer.
ie.p4: Drivers, vehicles and on-road decisions stay local. A dedicated offshore resource handles the structured back office — POD processing, customer updates, compliance and fatigue records, invoicing and data entry — often extending useful coverage outside standard Perth office hours.
ie.p5: Know the language: allocation, PODs, consignment notes, chain of responsibility, NHVAS, fatigue management, mass/dimension, 3PL, cold chain, linehaul. Know the tools: MyTrucking, TransVirtual, CargoWise, M&L, telematics. Speak to responsiveness, compliance and cash flow.

ie.h1: The labour market they live in
ie.p1: Training providers compete for both trainers/assessors and experienced compliance-savvy administrators, and both are scarce. Student administration is high-volume and deadline-driven, and turnover in reception and student-support roles disrupts the learner experience and the compliance trail at the same time.
ie.p2: An RTO runs on administration: enrolments and USI checks, LMS setup and updates, student communication, assessment records, compliance evidence, AVETMISS reporting, surveys and certificate issuance. When this slips, learner experience suffers, audit risk rises, and trainers get pulled into admin instead of teaching and assessing.
ie.p3: ASQA compliance and audit readiness are unforgiving, funding and reporting deadlines are fixed, and margins in private training are thin. Enrolment intakes create sharp peaks, and every incomplete evidence file or late certificate is both a learner and a compliance problem.
ie.p4: Trainer judgement, assessment decisions and compliance sign-off stay local. A dedicated offshore administrator handles the structured work — enrolment processing, LMS updates, student communication, evidence collation, survey follow-up and certificate preparation — improving consistency and easing pressure on the education and compliance team.
ie.p5: Know the language: RTO, ASQA, AVETMISS, USI, units of competency, training packages, LLN, RPL, VET Student Loans, evidence and validation. Know the tools: aXcelerate, VETtrak, Moodle, Canvas, Cloud Assess. Be precise that assessment and compliance judgement stay with the provider.

8.lede: A one-month campaign targeting WA strata, property-management and facilities-services businesses — managing a constant stream of maintenance, communication and compliance administration.
8.entry: Property administration assistant (maintenance coordination, arrears, invoicing, inspections)
8.whyPressure: Maintenance requests, contractor follow-up, owner and tenant communication, invoice processing, arrears follow-up, compliance records and inspection coordination are recurring, detailed and service-sensitive — and they quickly consume the day.
8.whyOpp: Offshore support works best where the role has clear processes, strong communication standards and access to the same systems as the local team — maintenance coordination, contractor compliance checks, owner updates, tenant communication, invoice coding, inspection booking and arrears administration — leaving relationship management local.
8.marketShape: Fragmented at the agency, strata and facilities-provider level. Focus on recurring operational administration across strata management, property management and facilities businesses.

ie.h1: The labour market they live in
ie.p1: Strata and property management are notoriously high-churn: managers and assistants burn out under portfolio loads and leave, taking knowledge with them. WA firms struggle to recruit and retain the administrators who keep portfolios moving, so vacancies pile pressure onto the managers who remain.
ie.p2: Every property and every scheme generates a stream of work: maintenance requests and contractor follow-up, owner and tenant communication, invoice coding, arrears follow-up, insurance and compliance records, inspection booking and meeting administration. When it backs up, owners and committees complain, maintenance stalls and managers spend their day firefighting rather than managing relationships.
ie.p3: Portfolios grow faster than headcount, fee pressure is constant, and service expectations from owners, tenants and committees are high. Trust-accounting and compliance obligations are strict. Every hour a manager spends coding invoices or chasing a contractor is an hour not spent retaining and winning management rights.
ie.p4: Owner, committee and tenant relationships stay with the local manager. A dedicated offshore administrator handles the process work — maintenance coordination, contractor compliance, arrears follow-up, invoice coding, inspection booking and communications — improving responsiveness and reducing backlog.
ie.p5: Know the language: strata schemes, levies, arrears, by-laws, AGMs/EGMs, common property, trust accounting, management rights, ingoing/outgoing inspections, work orders. Know the tools: StrataMaster, PropertyMe, Property Tree, Rockend, Console. Speak to responsiveness and manager retention.

9.lede: A one-month campaign targeting WA MSPs and business IT providers — where senior technicians lose time to repetitive tickets, documentation and user administration.
9.entry: Service-desk & documentation assistant (level 1 triage, documentation, monitoring)
9.whyPressure: Clients expect fast response times, strong documentation, careful user administration, monitoring, reporting and consistent ticket handling. Local technical staff often end up carrying work that could be structured into a dedicated support function.
9.whyOpp: Offshore support must be disciplined, secure and carefully scoped. The best use cases are level 1 service-desk support, ticket triage, documentation, asset register maintenance, user onboarding and offboarding, backup-check reporting and monitoring support — not uncontrolled technical access or unsupervised client management.
9.marketShape: MSP offshoring exists, but the WA SME MSP market is not controlled by one player. Position around disciplined, secure support — not cheap helpdesk.

ie.h1: The labour market they live in
ie.p1: IT talent is scarce and expensive everywhere, and WA MSPs compete with mining, government and national providers for engineers. Level 1 and service-desk staff are hard to retain — they get trained, then poached or promoted — leaving senior technicians covering repetitive tickets they should have handed down.
ie.p2: MSP economics depend on utilisation. When senior engineers spend time on repetitive tickets, documentation, asset registers, user onboarding/offboarding and backup checks, response times slip, documentation gaps grow and margin erodes. Poor documentation then makes every future ticket slower — a compounding problem.
ie.p3: Clients expect SLAs and fast response; security and compliance expectations keep rising; and margin pressure is constant. Cybersecurity obligations make careful, scoped access essential. Growth means more tickets and more onboarding — more low-complexity load on a team that should be doing higher-value project and security work.
ie.p4: Escalation, client trust and security decisions stay with the local team. A carefully scoped offshore resource handles level 1 triage, documentation, asset registers, onboarding/offboarding and backup-check reporting — improving ticket flow and documentation quality while senior engineers focus on complex and security work.
ie.p5: Know the language: MSP, MSSP, SLAs, L1/L2/L3, tickets and triage, RMM, PSA, onboarding/offboarding, MFA, backups, patching, SOC. Know the tools: ConnectWise, Autotask, Halo PSA, NinjaOne, Datto, Microsoft 365. Lead with discipline, security and scoping — never 'cheap helpdesk'.

10.lede: A one-month campaign targeting WA agribusinesses, food producers and regional exporters — lean teams stretched across operations and office work, especially through seasonal peaks.
10.entry: Operations & export administration assistant (logistics, export docs, supplier follow-up)
10.whyPressure: Logistics administration, supplier and customer follow-up, export documents, inventory updates, bookkeeping support, seasonal workforce admin and marketing coordination all need attention — especially during busy periods — and local staff are stretched across operational and office work at once.
10.whyOpp: The strongest use cases are practical support roles that reduce office pressure while keeping operational control local — export documentation, logistics admin, supplier and customer follow-up, inventory updates, bookkeeping support, seasonal labour admin and marketing coordination.
10.marketShape: Fragmented and regionally dispersed. Target growers, processors, packers, fisheries, wineries and food brands with export or wholesale complexity.

ie.h1: The labour market they live in
ie.p1: Regional WA businesses face the hardest labour market of all — small local populations, seasonal demand and strong competition for both field and office staff. Attracting an experienced administrator to a regional town is difficult and expensive, so owners and coordinators end up doing the office work themselves on top of operations.
ie.p2: Food and agribusiness run on documentation: export and logistics paperwork, supplier and customer follow-up, inventory and order administration, bookkeeping, seasonal workforce admin and marketing. During harvest, season or export windows this all peaks at once, and lean teams simply can't keep up — orders slip, documents delay shipments and cash flow suffers.
ie.p3: Work is intensely seasonal, margins are exposed to commodity prices and freight costs, and export compliance is exacting. Peaks demand surge capacity that's uneconomic to hire locally year-round, while off-peak periods can't justify permanent office headcount — a structural mismatch offshore support fits well.
ie.p4: Growers, production, quality and operational decisions stay with the local team. A dedicated offshore administrator handles the recurring office work — export docs, logistics admin, supplier/customer follow-up, inventory, bookkeeping support and marketing coordination — giving surge capacity through peaks without a permanent local overhead.
ie.p5: Know the language: export documentation, phytosanitary/health certificates, incoterms, bills of lading, packing lists, cold chain, wholesale and distribution, cellar door, seasonal labour. Know the tools: Xero/MYOB, CargoWise-adjacent, inventory and winery systems. Speak to surge capacity and follow-up discipline.
